The Hero Who Lost His Map

弄丢地图的英雄 · 639 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A library planned to adapt a classic work of fantasy fiction. Its legendary prince defeated a villain and escaped a curse with help from a fairy. Ro, the director, found the adventure enjoyable but its ending predictable. A spell could save the character from every consequence. She asked the cast whether the hero's own choice could matter. A talented actor said the hero would first have to admit losing a map. That seemed heroic enough.

2The creative team wrote a new script. A thief took a bag. The hero chased him, though his map had fallen behind a bench. One actor wanted a cruel gangster. Ro said the character could be a hungry child afraid of being treated as a liar. The encounter became more entertaining once the audience could see a mistake that the hero missed. An odd imitation of a cowboy voice turned out to be funnier than a threat.

3In the next episode the hero met a girl in a muddy cloak. The animated sketch made her look like an avatar from another realm. A child wanted to add a mythical monster. A second proposed that the girl be the creator of a strange universe. Ro kept her human. She knew the paths and was courageous enough to admit getting lost before. The story could make an extraordinary act believable by showing where the knowledge came from.

4A designer drew a queen's gate and a shadow above it. The effect looked horrible until a lamp revealed a branch. A child laughed at the weird illusion. The scary shape could still haunt the hero for a moment, then turn into a sign he could use. The heroine had to calm his rage and show him the way back. That reversal made a fight with a nasty creature seem less satisfying than one brief look at the right object.

5A comedian suggested a joke about a millionaire who bought a map and never learned to read it. It sounded childish when an actor called him a fool. Ro asked the heroine to tell a fable about her own foolishness instead. Her frank admission was admirable without turning her into a genius. The thief heard it, took pity on the hero, and returned the bag. That simple act of goodness let the plot change through a decision rather than an act of magic.

6A pupil wanted to retell it as a hilarious romantic comedy. Another suggested a mystery in which a ghost moved the map. Ro asked the narrator to keep the suspense until the gate, then show the audience the cause. That twist mattered more than a clever trick from a sitcom. Their imagination could change the style of the play. It still needed to preserve the moment when the hero recognized his own mistake.

7At the first performance a child asked after the show whether the prince had become worthy of his crown. Ro pointed to the map still lying behind the bench. The child could remember exactly when it had fallen. He also remembered which character had first admitted being wrong. A short adventure could make courage easier to see by giving a character something small to do in front of another person.

8The library kept both the tale and its adaptation. A child wanted to know which belonged with the comics. A local poet called the shadow fantastic. Ro said they could put the new script beside them if they wrote down its origin in local mythology. An amusing retelling could make a magical gate feel familiar, while a darker thriller could make it seem evil. Either version had to show why the hero went back. The pupil remembered the marvelous shadow. Ro asked him to tell what changed when the lamp came on. He found he could do it without repeating the original legend.

四级汇总词汇 · 38中文译文

弄丢地图的英雄

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1图书馆打算把一部经典奇幻作品改成戏。故事里，传奇王子在仙女的帮助下战胜坏人，摆脱了诅咒。导演罗觉得冒险有趣，结局却太好猜。咒语总能替主角摆平后果。她问演员，能不能让英雄靠自己的选择影响结局。一位有天分的演员说，那就先让英雄承认自己弄丢了地图。这件事本身就需要勇气。

2创作团队写了新剧本。一个小偷拿走了包，英雄追了上去，地图却早就掉在长椅后面。一位演员想把小偷演成残忍的匪徒。罗觉得可以让他成为一个饥饿的孩子，因为怕被人当成骗子而不敢说实话。观众看得出英雄还没察觉的错误，这场相遇因此更有意思。有人怪腔怪调地学了一声牛仔，效果比威胁人的台词还好笑。

3下一幕，英雄遇到一个披着泥披风的女孩。动画草图让她看起来像来自另一世界的化身。有个孩子想加一头神话怪兽，另一个建议让女孩创造一个奇异宇宙。罗保留了她普通人的身份。女孩熟悉小路，也有勇气承认自己曾在这里迷路。只要说明她是怎样熟悉这些路的，观众就会相信，她真能做出一件了不起的事。

4布景师画了一扇王后的大门，上面有一片影子。那片影子原本很吓人，直到灯光照出一根树枝。一个孩子笑起这古怪的错觉。可怕的形状可以先把英雄吓一下，接着又变成他能利用的标记。女主角要平息他的怒气，告诉他怎么往回走。有了这个转折，观众看一眼真正的东西，就比看英雄打一场怪兽更过瘾。

5一位喜剧演员提议讲个笑话，说有个百万富翁买了地图，始终没学会看。演员管他叫傻瓜时，笑话听起来有点幼稚。罗改请女主角用一个寓言讲自己做过的傻事。她大方承认错误，这一点就值得佩服。小偷听见了，对英雄生出一点同情，于是把包还给了他。这个简单的善举改变了故事走向，事情也终于有了靠人物自己的决定而出现的转机。

6一个学生想把这段改成爆笑的爱情喜剧，另一个想写成鬼魂挪走地图的悬疑故事。罗让讲述者把悬念保留到大门那里，再让观众看到真正的原因。这个转折比情景喜剧里随手借来的点子更重要。想象力可以改变戏的风格，英雄发现自己犯错的那一刻仍然要让观众看到。

7第一次演完后，一个孩子问，王子现在配得上自己的王冠了吗？罗指了指还在长椅后面的地图。孩子想得起地图是什么时候掉的，也记得第一个承认错误的是谁。在别人面前完成一件小事，就可以让一段短短的冒险把勇气讲清楚。

8图书馆同时保留了原故事和改编版。一个孩子问，哪个版本能放在漫画旁边。本地诗人觉得那片影子奇妙极了。罗说，只要在新剧本上标清它来自当地神话，也可以放过去。好笑的讲法可以让魔法大门显得亲切，阴暗的惊悚版可以把它写得邪恶。但两个版本都得交代英雄为什么往回走。学生记得那片精彩的影子。罗请他讲讲灯亮时发生了什么。他发现，自己可以直接把那段讲清楚。
